Summary: Where files live while the project runs, and how a team shares them across islands.
Picks: ST-01+ST-02=The suite your institution already provides. Pick one for research data: two suites double the places data can hide. | PG-01=A short data management plan fixes formats, licences and the repository before the first file exists.
Guidance: Working storage is not an archive. When the project ends or a paper comes out, the data moves to a repository: see Share and publish.

Summary: Surveys, forms and fieldwork, online or offline.
Picks: CO-03=Free, works offline in the field, and the questionnaire itself is a reusable XLSForm. | CO-01+CO-02=Whichever your institution provides, for a short form with no sensitive questions.
Guidance: If you collect personal data, check what your ethics review requires before you choose a tool, and where the tool stores the answers.

Summary: Statistics, qualitative coding, dashboards and data science.
Streams: Quantitative analysis; Qualitative analysis; Data science and visualisation
Picks: QA-05=Free, scripted and reproducible, and the language the DCDC courses teach. | QA-03=Point-and-click like SPSS, free and open source, and it opens .sav files. | QL-06=Open-source qualitative coding that moves whole projects to and from NVivo and ATLAS.ti.
Guidance: Whatever the tool, keep the steps: a script, a syntax file or a saved workflow, so the analysis can be run again.

Summary: Make your data and outputs findable, citable and reusable once a project or paper is done.
Picks: PA-01=Accepts any research output, gives it a DOI, and hosts the DCDC-Network community. | ID-03=Your own persistent identifier, so your outputs stay linked to you wherever they are published.
Guidance: Look first for a repository in your own discipline, through re3data or FAIRsharing. Where none fits, use a general repository such as Zenodo, or your institution's own repository, such as the University of Aruba's Open Knowledge Repository. Share the data at the same time as the preprint or the article.
Link label: Sharing research data, the DCDC two-pager

Summary: Version control, open lessons, and documents built from code.
Picks: CD-01=The usual place to share code. Linked to Zenodo, every release gets a DOI automatically. | CD-05=An open, non-profit alternative for public work. Releases go to Zenodo by hand. | CD-04=How the DCDC courses are built, so a lesson can be shared and adapted across islands.
Guidance: Archive a release in Zenodo whenever code or a lesson is cited or taught.

Summary: What happens to your data when you use an AI assistant.
Picks: AI-01+AI-02=The assistant inside your institution's Microsoft or Google account, covered by the institution's agreement. | AI-06+AI-07=For confidential material: a model that runs on your own computer, so nothing leaves the device.
Guidance: Never paste personal or confidential data into a personal AI account.
